name: Dinh Cau
kicker: Temple on the rocks at Dương Đông
summary: Rock temple in Dương Đông: stand on the point at sunset, then watch the squid boats light the water. The bureau says the temple was built in 1937 for Cậu, a deity over the waters, to protect boats in heavy weather. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism also calls it a pagoda and a lighthouse shrine to the goddess of the sea. Both names and both deities stay. The visit is the late afternoon.
getThere: On the Dương Đông shore, at the north end of Bãi Trường
heroCaption: Dinh Cậu on the rocks, with the shrine stairs and the harbour water
body: Stand at Dinh Cậu for the sunset, then stay as the beach empties and the squid boats light the water. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the temple was built in 1937 for Cậu, a deity with authority over the waters, to protect boats in heavy weather, and that the lights on the water after dark look like a city. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism calls the building Dinh Cau Temple and Dinh Cau Pagoda. The nature account says sailors pray to the goddess of the sea. The day account says the lighthouse doubles as a shrine to the Goddess of the Sea, with the view over the harbour. All three names stay, and both deities stay.

Bãi Trường’s bureau page starts the long beach at Mũi Dinh Cậu, so the temple is the north end of that sand, in Dương Đông. The night account closes the streets near the rock temple to traffic from 5 pm until midnight for the market. Come for the light, then walk into the stalls if the catch is the dinner.

figures.caption: The shrine porch at Dinh Cậu, under the dragons and the tiled roof
figures.alt: The painted shrine porch of Dinh Cau temple on Phu Quoc

gettingThere: Dinh Cậu stands on the Dương Đông shore, at Mũi Dinh Cậu, where Bãi Trường begins. The bureau places the town in the west-centre of the island. Walk to it from a room in town. From a room on the long beach, the temple is the north end of the sand.

legs.heading: From Dương Đông
legs.body: The temple is on the town shore. Come in the late afternoon and stay into the dark for the squid-boat lights.

legs.heading: From Long Beach
legs.body: Bãi Trường starts at Mũi Dinh Cậu. The temple is that north end. The night market streets beside it close to traffic from 5 pm until midnight.
